one_sentence: This document argues that Christianity uniquely satisfies all eight boundary conditions derived from physics, making it the uniquely correct worldview.
executive_summary: This document presents an isomorphism record (ISO-024) that maps the mathematical concept of a system of eight simultaneous equations with a unique solution onto the theological claim of Christian exclusivity. The core claim is that eight boundary conditions (BCs) can be derived from physics, and Christianity is the only worldview that satisfies all eight, while other major worldviews (Islam, Buddhism, Hinduism) fail specific BCs. The document includes a detailed mapping, tests (including a swap test and falsification criteria), and an honest assessment highlighting severe risks of confirmation bias, circularity, and oversimplification of diverse traditions. It concludes that the ISO cannot be validated without independent audit of the BC derivation and fair evaluation of non-Christian worldviews, and recommends specific actions before status upgrade.
short_summary: This document is an isomorphism record (ISO-024) that applies a constraint-satisfaction framework from mathematics to evaluate worldviews. The core structural claim is that Christianity uniquely satisfies all eight boundary conditions derived from physics, while other worldviews fail specific ones. Key evidence includes a spreadsheet analysis and a mapping of mathematical elements to theological concepts, but the document itself acknowledges severe risks of confirmation bias and circularity. This matters because it attempts to provide a physics-derived rational warrant for Christian exclusivity, but its validity depends entirely on independent audit of the boundary condition derivation and fair representation of other traditions.
